title: Theodoretus Mopsuestenus
author: Incertus
source: Translated by Claude from tmp794.tmp794.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

passages.original: Simul admonere volens Julianum, ex episcopo oppidi Eclanensis haereticum Pelagianum seu Coeles- tianum, hunc secutum esse Theodorum, ad quem, peragratis terris, et exarato mari, atque Oriente lu- strato, cum sociis et participibus et συνταλαιπώροις suis, magno nisu, tamquam ad Christianorum dogmatum praedicatum magistrum, tetendit, ut de haeresi Pela- giana, seu Coelestiana, quam defendendam et sequen- dam suscepit, ab ipso confirmaretur, atque inde ve- lut instructior, octo, contra fidem catholicam potius quam contra sanctae memoriae Augustinum, volumina illa, ut putat, prudentissima conderet.
passages.english: At the same time, he wished to point out that Julian, formerly bishop of the town of Eclanum and now a Pelagian or Caelestian heretic, had followed this Theodore. To him, after traveling across lands, ploughing through the sea and going all over the East, Julian made his way with great effort, together with his companions, associates and *syntalaipōroi* (fellow-sufferers), as to a renowned teacher of Christian doctrines, in order to be confirmed by him in the Pelagian or Caelestian heresy, which he had undertaken to defend and follow, and so, as if better instructed from that source, to compose those eight volumes, most wise as he thinks, against the Catholic faith rather than against Augustine of holy memory.
passages.notes: Scanning splits (Coeles- tianum, lu- strato, Pela- giana, sequen- dam, ve- lut) were read as whole words. The Greek συνταλαιπώροις ('fellow-sufferers') stands in the Latin text. 'praedicatum' is taken as 'renowned, celebrated'. The work label 'Theodoretus Mopsuestenus' presumably refers to Theodore of Mopsuestia.
